title: From Integrated Communication to Algorithmic Orchestration: Marketing Communication, Advertising Research, and the Digital Transformation of Persuasion, 2000–2026
content: Marketing communication has undergone a structural transformation comparable in magnitude to the television revolution of the mid-twentieth century. This paper develops an integrative, qualitative analysis of marketing communication in the age of digital media across the 26-year period from 2000 to 2026, pursuing four questions: how digitalization has reconfigured the conceptual and operational architecture of the field; what role advertising now performs within that architecture; how the discipline relates, intellectually and institutionally, to the older tradition of advertising research and practice; and which research gaps most urgently demand scholarly attention. Methodologically, the study combines an integrative literature review with reflexive thematic analysis, triangulated against harmonized statistical series (ITU/World Bank, IAB/PwC, WPP Media) and industry audits. A structured review of 36 studies 20 foundational studies published between 2015 and 2023, and 16 studies published between 2024 and 2026—anchors the analysis at the research frontier, spanning integration and journey theory, causal effectiveness measurement, privacy regulation, influencer marketing, and generative artificial intelligence. The analysis traces the field's development through six historical stages, compares three research traditions whose convergence now defines the study of communication effectiveness, and documents an accountability crisis evidenced by programmatic supply-chain leakage, deflationary causal estimates of advertising effects, and signal loss under privacy regulation. Four overarching themes emerge: the migration from linear message delivery to dialogic orchestration; the datafication and algorithmic mediation of persuasion; the rising centrality of trust, privacy, and ethics; and the convergence-within-fragmentation of advertising. The paper contributes a stage model of the field's development, a comparative framework of research traditions and measurement approaches, two synthesis matrices of recent evidence, a consolidated taxonomy of research gaps, a concise analytical discussion, and a prioritized program of ten recommended research streams with implications for managers, regulators, and scholars.
